subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 5: Culture – Good manners around the world
outcomes: I can talk about good manners in Oman, the UK, China and Japan.
I can compare good manners in Oman with another country.
I can write manners with It's polite to …, You should … and In Oman, you must ….

tf.s: In the UK, people say thank you to the bus driver when they get off.
tf.why: Yes! The text says this about the UK.

tf.s: In China, it's polite to finish everything on your plate.
tf.why: In China, it's rude. It means you didn't get enough food.

tf.s: In Oman, you take off your shoes when you go inside someone's house.
tf.why: Right! This is good manners in Oman.

tf.s: In Japan, it's polite to laugh with your mouth wide open.
In some parts of Asia, it's better to give a gentle handshake.
tf.why: Yes! A gentle handshake is better there.

tf.s: In Oman, men give a gentle handshake.
tf.why: In Oman, men give a firm handshake.

tf.s: "It's polite to say thank you" is a correct sentence.
Good manners are the same in every country.
tf.why: Some manners are different around the world.

tf.s: "You should listen to older people" gives advice.
In Two stars and a wish, a star is something good about the work.
tf.why: Right! The wish is something to make better.

boxes.q: Change into advice: listen to older people.
o: You should listen to older people.
You listen should to older people.

boxes.q: In Oman, you ___ take off your shoes inside a house.
boxes.why: It is a rule of good manners in Oman.
Please and thank you are good manners everywhere in the text.

boxes.q: What is the opposite of polite?
What is the speaking tip in the project?
boxes.why: A smile helps people listen to you.

boxes.q: A strong handshake is a ___ handshake.
A soft handshake is a ___ handshake.
What does the good manners book need?
o: a cover, a title and three manners
boxes.why: The product is a folded book with a cover, a title and three manners.

o: Please can I have some water?

hunt.q: Rude to laugh with your mouth wide open
Take a small ___ when you visit.
Take off your ___ in an Omani house.
Say this to the bus driver in the UK

mcq.q: Where is it better to give a gentle handshake?
mcq.why: The text says a gentle handshake is better in some parts of Asia.

mcq.q: Which phrase can start a rule in the good manners book?
mcq.why: The project uses In Oman, you must …, You should … and It's polite to …

mcq.q: Which countries do we read about in this lesson?
o: the UK, Oman, China and Japan
the UK, France, Italy and Oman
mcq.why: The text talks about the UK, Oman, China and Japan.

mcq.q: Name one good manner in Oman.
o: Laugh with your mouth open at people.
mcq.why: Listening to older people is good manners in Oman.

mcq.q: Write good advice for school with "You should …".
o: You should say good morning to your teacher.
You should be rude to your teacher.
You should to say good morning.
mcq.why: You should + verb: You should say …

mcq.q: You visit a friend's house in Oman. What should you do at the door?
mcq.why: In Oman, we take off our shoes inside a house.

mcq.q: You eat dinner with a family in China. What is good manners there?
o: Don't finish everything on your plate.
mcq.why: In China, finishing everything means you didn't get enough food.

mcq.q: Why is it rude in China to finish everything on your plate?
o: It means you didn't get enough food.
It means the food is cold.
It means you want to go home.
mcq.why: An empty plate says the host didn't give you enough.

mcq.q: Which good manner is the same in Oman and the UK?
o: laughing with your mouth wide open
mcq.why: Please and thank you are polite in both countries.

mcq.q: A group's book has beautiful pictures but very small writing. Which is the best wish?
mcq.why: A wish says what can be better; the pictures are already a star.
